title: Pre-flight judges by need, ours first
why: decisions/0163's note of 2026-11-17, the source map (Jason: "we should have backups for sources/apis if one fails"; "ok on starting your part"). 1. Two new groups: What the engine needs (21 needs, needed for launch) and What the site needs (22, shown, optional for the engine's launch). Each need lists its sources in order, ours first: our own copies (open_places, npi_orgs, irs_orgs, rec_places, landmarks, zip_coordinates, travel_legs, source_facts, heritage_facts, stock_images and more) checked for rows and freshness, then each outside source by its own line. 2. A need is ✓ when its first source works, amber "on a backup" when a later one does (or when its fallback always works, like keyword search or estimated drive times), ✗ only when nothing works. A need with one source says "No backup yet" with the planned backup. 3. Each workflow is now judged by its needs instead of each company, so a company that's down but has a working backup no longer holds a workflow; services are needed for launch only for what everything stands on (Bluehost, Railway, GitHub). 4. The report marks a need on a backup as BKUP. The paid-backup overrides and the workflows' own fallbacks (W1 reading open_places before Overpass first) are the next builds.

items: No new fatal errors in the logs
